title: Sample-half-inserted quantum interferometer
authors: Wei Li, Tao Xie, Yu-Hang Luo, Kang Zheng, Meiyu Peng, Hui Yang, Chunling Ding, Chen-Zhi Yuan, Omar S. Magana-Loaiza, Keyu Xia, Ryosuke Shimizu, Hui Jing, Chenglong You, Rui-Bo Jin
abstract: Quantum technologies have been widely recognized as unprecedented opportunities for ultra-high precision metrology. As a celebrated example in modern quantum optics, the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometer is well-known for enabling temporal resolutions on the attosecond scale. However, the relatively low Fisher information per trial in ordinary HOM measurements typically necessitates tens of thousands of repetitions to achieve such precision. Here, we propose and demonstrate a sample-half-inserted HOM (SHOM) interferometer, which enhances the Fisher information by five orders of magnitude in a single interference event. By introducing an asymmetric photon-sample interaction, the SHOM configuration produces a distinctive dip-bump-dip interference structure, converting what was previously viewed as an artifact into a helpful metrological resource. Experimentally, we measured the optical path difference with an average precision of 4.09 nm (13.63 as) and an average accuracy of 1.22 nm (4.07 as) using $O(10^7)$ photons. Our results establish SHOM interferometry as an efficient phase-insensitive approach, not only paving the way toward practical quantum-enhanced thickness measurement for transparent materials, but also serving as an elegant strategy to improve the performance of various quantum devices.
summary: The paper introduces the Sample-Half-Inserted HOM (SHOM) interferometer as a novel technique to dramatically improve measurement precision in quantum interferometry. By exploiting an asymmetric photon-sample interaction, SHOM enhances the Fisher information by five orders of magnitude over standard methods. This allows for achieving nanoscale measurements with significantly fewer photons, paving the way for practical quantum-enhanced metrology.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enhance the precision of optical path difference measurements using Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry, which typically suffers from low Fisher information per measurement trial.
main_result: The proposed Sample-Half-Inserted HOM (SHOM) interferometer enhances the Fisher information by five orders of magnitude compared to standard HOM. Experimentally, this allowed achieving nanoscale precision ($13.63 	ext{ as}$) using significantly fewer photons ($O(10^7)$).
method: The authors developed and experimentally demonstrated the SHOM configuration, which introduces an asymmetric photon-sample interaction leading to a unique dip-bump-dip interference pattern.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum interferometer utilizing two-photon quantum interference (HOM effect) enhanced by modifying the sample interaction to create the SHOM setup. Theoretical models for coincidence probabilities ($	ext{P}_{	ext{SHOM}}$) and precision estimation via Fisher Information were employed.
key_observables: Coincidence counts, optical path difference/time delay ($T$), interference patterns (dip-bump-dip structure), and calculated Fisher information ($F$).
important_parameters: Precision of $4.09 	ext{ nm}$ ($\approx 13.63 	ext{ as}$) and accuracy of $1.22 	ext{ nm}$ ($\approx 4.07 	ext{ as}$) achieved with $O(10^7)$ photons.
main_assumptions: The fundamental limitation overcome is the low Fisher information inherent to standard HOM schemes; the technique assumes that the asymmetric interaction can be reliably modeled and measured.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the concept of SHOM setup and compares coincidence probabilities ($	ext{P}_{	ext{HOM}}$ vs $	ext{P}_{	ext{SHOM}}$). Figure 2 shows experimental results, including HOM/SHOM patterns varying with temperature, resulting sinusoidal count variations, and calculated Fisher information.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitation of standard HOM interferometry, proposes the SHOM enhancement via asymmetric interaction, derives the necessary mathematical models for coincidence probabilities and Fisher Information, presents experimental validation showing superior precision, and concludes by discussing the broad applicability of the SHOM technique to other quantum metrology tasks.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally validated method to boost the sensitivity of quantum optical measurements beyond standard limits by engineering the interaction geometry, which is highly relevant for developing practical quantum sensors in AMO physics and quantum optics.
